preconditions.expression: all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in x) and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in y)
preconditions.description: Both input strings x and y consist only of lowercase Latin letters.
The lengths of x and y are between 1 and 1000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: stdout == str(sum(f(l1, r1, l2, r2) for l1 in range(1, len(x)+1) for r1 in range(l1, len(x)+1) for l2 in range(1, len(y)+1) for r2 in range(l2, len(y)+1)) % 998244353)
postconditions.description: The output is the sum of f(l1, r1, l2, r2) over all valid 1 ≤ l1 ≤ r1 ≤ |x| and 1 ≤ l2 ≤ r2 ≤ |y|, modulo 998244353, where f(l1, r1, l2, r2) is the number of different merging sequences of x[l1-1:r1] and y[l2-1:r2] that produce chaotic merges.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= l1 <= r1 <= len(x) for l1 in range(1, len(x)+1) for r1 in range(l1, len(x)+1)) and all(1 <= l2 <= r2 <= len(y) for l2 in range(1, len(y)+1) for r2 in range(l2, len(y)+1))
postconditions.description: The summation iterates over all valid non-empty substring ranges for x and y.

postconditions.expression: lambda l1, r1, l2, r2: (lambda x_sub, y_sub: sum(1 for a in product([0]*len(x_sub), [1]*len(y_sub)) if is_chaotic_merge(x_sub, y_sub, a)))
postconditions.description: For each substring pair (x[l1-1:r1], y[l2-1:r2]), f(l1, r1, l2, r2) counts the number of merging sequences a (combinations of 0s and 1s) that produce a chaotic merge z, where z is chaotic if for all i from 2 to |z|, z[i-1] != z[i].

postconditions.expression: lambda x_sub, y_sub, a: (lambda z: all(z[i-1] != z[i] for i in range(2, len(z))))(merge(x_sub, y_sub, a))
postconditions.description: A merge z is chaotic if no two adjacent characters in z are the same. The merge is constructed by appending characters from x_sub and y_sub in the order specified by the merging sequence a.
